correctness.rationale: The witness condition immediately bounds omitted vertices by \(|U_A|,|U_B|\le2\), giving \(|S|\ge2n-4\). At equality, the unique possible witnesses across each two-vertex omitted side force the two omitted index pairs to be disjoint. Conversely, disjoint omitted pairs give four explicit private witnesses. The selected subgraph is connected for every \(n\ge4\). Exhaustive verification through \(n=7\) reproduces both ordinary and connected-super minimum layers exactly.

originality.rationale: The strongest direct prior comparison is the published complete-bipartite formula \(\gamma_{\mathrm{sp}}(K_{n,n})=2n-2\). It does not imply the value after deleting a perfect matching, because the super-domination witness condition changes with edge deletion. Primary full-text sources on ordinary and connected super domination were inspected, together with the 2022/2024 graph-classes-and-enumeration treatment. No crown or matching-deletion theorem was located, and complete-multipartite results do not cover crown graphs.
residual_risks: A differently phrased or non-indexed crown-graph treatment may exist.
The n=3 boundary has a different minimum-family structure.
The theorem does not address arbitrary matching deletions or the full super-domination polynomial.

value.rationale: Crown graphs are the canonical perfect-matching deletion of balanced complete bipartite graphs. The result shows a sharp two-unit drop from the known \(K_{n,n}\) value and simultaneously proves that the connected-super constraint has zero extra cost. The exact disjoint-pair classification and count \(\binom n2\binom{n-2}{2}\) expose the full equality structure, making the result a natural edge-deletion sensitivity benchmark rather than an isolated numerical computation.
